explanation: Most fungi are multicellular. Multicellular fungi possess a thallus or body structure called a mycelium, which is made of a network of filaments known as hyphae. This network provides a high surface-area-to-volume ratio, facilitating absorption. Hyphae can wall off as they grow (septate) or remain unpartitioned (nonseptate). Fungi lack chloroplasts and have cell walls composed of chitin rather than cellulose. They are non-motile, meaning their only movement is the growth extension of their hyphae toward a food source.
